reproFailure: AssertionError: expected 'coverage-verified' not to be 'coverage-verified' // Object.is equality (red 3/3 at base; extended file also red on unitsMatched 'expected 1 to be +0' and delta unitsCompared 'expected 1 to be +0'; final file 5 failed | 1 passed at base, 3/3 runs)
assumptions: The two repro branches reproduce the same scenario; kept one file (the standalone ts/test/guardian-coverage-cross-package-suffix.test.ts from repro/coverage-cross-package-suffix) and ported the unitsMatched assertion from repro/bf-a3-cross-package-suffix-bind into it, so the bug's repro lives in one place instead of being appended to the 1400-line guardian-coverage.test.ts.
Added a same-package positive and a coverage-delta case to the same file, since the issue names the delta as a shared consumer of the matching semantics.

Investigation found a second shape of the same root cause the issue did not name: once a key is anchored to pkg-a/src/index.ts, a changed root-level src/index.ts still bound it by suffix (and at base it bound by EXACT match on the raw key). Treated as in scope, not adjacent: the fix makes an anchored entry exact-match-only (FileCoverage.anchored), with its own reproducing test.
Anchoring is per top-level key group via the existing #883 anchorPrefix, not per key, so a stale report whose group still has one existing file anchors its deleted entries too.
Entries that cannot be anchored (absolute keys, or a group none of whose files exist) keep the existing suffix fallback unchanged; tightening those is out of scope.
The public resolveFromReport(units, reportPath) API takes no repoRoot and so is left un-anchored; only the ladder (resolveCoverage/resolveCoverageWithInput) and the delta are fixed.

Anchoring code moved from report-tier.ts into a new ts/src/guardian/diff-coverage/report-anchor.ts, because adding it in place put report-tier.ts over the 300-line check-perf file-length threshold (a new perf finding). report-tier re-exports it so orchestrator gains no import (a direct import added a coupling finding).
